findings.condition: Four PRs (PR-1230, PR-1018, PR-1300, PR-1265) were merged to main with only the author as the sole approver, providing no independent review.
findings.criteria: Policy Section 3.1: 'At least one approver other than the author must approve the pull request before it is merged.'
findings.cause: Pull requests were merged without enforcing the segregation of duties requirement; either the merge was allowed despite lacking proper approval or approvals were not properly recorded.
findings.effect: Production changes were deployed without independent verification, increasing the risk of unreviewed code entering production and potential quality/security issues going undetected.
findings.recommendation: Enforce branch protection rules to require at least one approver other than the author before allowing merges to main. Implement automated checks to block merges that do not meet this requirement. Review existing PRs to identify and remediate similar exceptions.

findings.effect: Lack of audit trail for emergency changes; unable to verify retroactive approval within 2 business days; control objective not met.
findings.recommendation: Implement system controls to prevent emergency deploys without a linked change ticket, and establish a remediation process to document and approve retroactively for existing gaps.

findings.condition: Critical vulnerability VULN-0003 (CVE-2026-29275) required 47 days to remediate from opening (2025-11-01) to closing (2025-12-18), exceeding the 30-day SLA limit. No risk acceptance ticket was associated with this vulnerability.
findings.criteria: Policy section 2.2: 'Critical vulnerabilities are remediated within 30 calendar days of being opened.' Section 2.3: Exceptions require an approved, unexpired risk acceptance ticket signed by Security Lead and CTO.
findings.cause: The vulnerability remained open beyond the 30-day window without obtaining an approved risk acceptance before the deadline.
findings.effect: The organization failed to meet its documented vulnerability management SLA for critical vulnerabilities, potentially leaving production assets exposed to known security risks for an extended period.
findings.recommendation: Implement automated tracking and alerts for critical vulnerabilities approaching the 30-day threshold. Establish a process to obtain risk acceptance approvals before SLA expiration when remediation cannot be completed in time.
